transcript.content: Hello, please have a seat. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I’m here because... honestly, for months now I’ve been trying to get people to understand that my husband’s family is quietly messing with our money and our good name. It's happening everywhere. Like, these little billing errors will just show up at my work. I do billing and posting, you know, and we actually just got these new ergonomic chairs in the office, which I thought would really help my sciatica. I’ve had this awful shooting pain down my left leg ever since my cousin's wedding a few years ago. I wore these horrible silver heels that just completely threw out my alignment, and I haven't been the same since. 

But anyway, I see the errors on the accounts, and then someone at church will suddenly act funny toward me, too. We had a potluck last Sunday and I brought a green bean casserole, and the pastor's wife just completely avoided me. She usually always asks for my recipe because I use the real crispy onions on top, the name brand, not the cheap store brand that gets soggy. But no matter what records anyone pulls up about the accounts or what anyone tries to tell me, I know it all ties back to his family.
How has your sleep been lately?

My sleep? Um... I guess it's fine. I haven't really noticed anything unusual with it. I mean, I try to get to bed at a normal time, and I actually just started using this new lavender laundry detergent on our sheets. It's the one with the purple cap? 

My sister-in-law, Brenda, she was the one who told me lavender is supposed to be calming. But honestly, she buys all her stuff from those people on Facebook who sell things out of their living rooms, you know what I mean? She tried to corner me into buying these expensive essential oils from her at Thanksgiving. I finally just had to tell her, "Brenda, I am not paying forty dollars for a tiny little bottle of peppermint water." So I just bought the detergent at the regular grocery store instead. It was actually on a buy-one-get-one-free special, which was great because, I swear, every time I go to the store lately, the total is just completely outrageous. I don't know how people with big families afford to eat these days.
Have you ever heard voices or sounds when no one else was around?

Voices? No, no, nothing like that. I don't hear things that aren't there. Although, honestly, my hearing has been a little sensitive lately, mostly just because our neighbors got this new dog. It’s some kind of terrier mix, I think? And it just barks at everything. A leaf blows across the driveway, and it’s out there yapping. 

I actually tried talking to the neighbor about it—his name is Gary, he works at the hardware store downtown—and he just brushed me off. Said the dog is still a puppy and learning. But I told him, "Gary, a puppy needs structure." I used to have a golden retriever, Buster, and we took him to obedience school when he was just four months old. The trainer there was this older lady, Mrs. Higgins, and she always said a tired dog is a good dog. We used to walk Buster twice a day, all the way down to the park and back. They just redid the playground at that park, by the way. Put in one of those fancy soft rubber floors instead of wood chips, which I guess is safer, but it smells terrible in the summer when the sun beats down on it. Anyway, no, I don't hear voices. Just that dog.
Have you ever felt like thoughts that were not your own were being put into your head?

Thoughts put into my head? No, I don't... I don't know what you mean by that. My thoughts are my own. I mean, I do get a lot of ideas when I'm watching those home improvement shows on the weekends. My husband and I, we've been talking about redoing the backsplash in the kitchen for years now. The current one is this awful beige tile from the nineties, with these little painted fruit baskets on random tiles. It's so dated. 

I actually saw this beautiful subway tile at the home center last week. It was a pale seafoam green, which I think would look so nice with our cabinets. But my husband, he thinks we should just paint the cabinets white instead. He's always trying to find the cheapest way to do things, which, I mean, I get it, especially with his family messing with our accounts like I told you. But you can't just slap a coat of paint on cheap oak cabinets and expect it to look like a magazine. You have to sand them down, use a good primer... my uncle Bob was a carpenter, and he always said the prep work is ninety percent of the job. He built this incredible birdhouse for me when I was a little girl, looked exactly like a Victorian mansion. It even had tiny little shingles on the roof. But no, I don't have anyone putting thoughts in my head. Just my own ideas for the kitchen.
